The core-periphery model of development is a theory that explains the uneven distribution of economic development across different regions of a country or the world. It suggests that there is a hierarchy of regions, with the core regions being the most developed and the peripheral regions being the least developed. The spread effect in the core-periphery model refers to the process by which the development of the core regions spreads to the peripheral regions, leading to a more even distribution of economic development across the country or the world.
A. Congestion in the core: This is a spread effect in the core-periphery model of development. Congestion in the core refers to the high density of people, businesses, and infrastructure in the core regions, which can lead to increased costs and reduced efficiency. This can make it difficult for peripheral regions to catch up with the core regions in terms of economic development.
B. High cost of labor in the core: This is a spread effect in the core-periphery model of development. High cost of labor in the core refers to the fact that the core regions have a higher cost of labor than the peripheral regions. This can make it more difficult for peripheral regions to attract and retain skilled workers, which can limit their ability to develop.
C. High density in the core: This is a spread effect in the core-periphery model of development. High density in the core refers to the fact that the core regions have a higher population density than the peripheral regions. This can make it more difficult for peripheral regions to develop, as they may lack the resources and infrastructure to support a large population.
D. More infrastructure in the core: This is NOT a spread effect in the core-periphery model of development. More infrastructure in the core refers to the fact that the core regions have more infrastructure, such as roads, bridges, and airports, than the peripheral regions. This can make it easier for the core regions to develop, but it does not necessarily lead to a more even distribution of economic development across the country or the world.</think>
<answer>A</answer>
